title: Craniofacial growth: child and adolescent faces

queue.claim: The cornea (visible iris diameter) reaches adult size (~11.5–12 mm) by about age 2–3 and is ~9.5–10.5 mm at birth, so it can be the metric scale anchor for children aged 3 and over (prior N(11.8, 0.5–0.8) mm).
queue.query: corneal diameter growth infancy childhood age reaches adult size horizontal visible iris diameter

queue.claim: Percent-of-adult-size by age (e.g. face height n–gn ~76–81 % and face width zy–zy ~82–86 % at 6 y), with maturation around 13–15 y in females and 15–18+ y in males (Farkas growth series).
queue.query: Farkas Posnick Hreczko 1992 growth patterns of the face morphometric study age of maturation facial height width percentage adult

queue.claim: Eyeball axial length is ~16.5–17.5 mm at birth, ~20–21 mm at 1 y, ~22.3–23 mm at 6 y and near the adult ~23.5–24 mm by 10–13 y. IPD runs ~37–42 mm at birth to ~49–53 mm at 6 y.

queue.claim: FaceBase 3D Facial Norms provides sex-specific 3D growth curves (ages 3–40). Summary landmark data are openly downloadable, and individual data need a Data Access Request.
